# Issue #773: TASK-C551-1: the gallery's SVG renders are regenerated by one scripted command, so a render cannot drift from the circuit it depicts
- Lens: adversarial
- Date: 2026-08-08
- Reviewer: Claude Sonnet 5
- Verdict: needs-rework

## Summary of the ask

One scripted command renders an SVG + caption per circuit in the Examples set via the existing `-i out.svg` batch export, pulling captions from #548's metadata; CI regenerates and fails on drift. Part of feature #551 (gallery), ordered after task #768 (TASK-C548-3, caption/exercise metadata).

## Findings, most severe first

**1. [High] AC2's byte-diff CI check assumes a determinism guarantee the codebase explicitly disclaims for the exact export path this task is scoped to use.**
`test/jls/SvgExportTest.java:16-25` states in the class javadoc: "Deliberately no full-document golden - text layout coordinates depend on the JDK's font metrics, which differ across machines (the same reason `CliImageExportTest` avoids pixel goldens)." That comment is about the screen-styled `-i out.svg` export (issue #154) — the very export #773 AC1 says to use. The project already built and shipped a *separate* feature, #536 (FEAT-C24-1, band_mw 4-6), whose entire job is to make SVG export byte-identical across platforms via "a bundled deterministic font path — no OS font fallback in the render" (#536 AC2, `FigureDeterminismTest`). #773 (band_mw 0.5-1) quietly requires that same guarantee — "CI ... fails when a committed render differs from the freshly generated one" is meaningless unless renders are byte-stable across whatever machine committed the file and whatever machine CI runs on — for the *un-hardened* export path, with a budget roughly 1/8th of what the project itself estimated the determinism work costs. Concretely: a contributor regenerates and commits gallery SVGs from a local build (different OS/JDK-patch/font-package versions than the `ubuntu-latest` CI runner, per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`), and AC2 goes red on pure environment drift, not circuit drift — exactly the failure mode `SvgExportTest` was written to avoid asserting on.
Recommendation: either (a) scope AC2 to a structural/semantic diff (e.g., re-render and compare drawn geometry/text content, not raw bytes) instead of a byte diff, (b) pin generation to a single environment (a CI-only regeneration step, never locally, with local diffs advisory) so "committed vs. regenerated" is always same-machine, or (c) make #773 formally depend on #536's determinism work and update `ordering_after` accordingly instead of `[TASK-C548-3]` only.

**2. [Medium] The task's prerequisite chain is four issues deep and none of it exists in the repository yet — understated in the issue body.**
`ordering_after: [TASK-C548-3]` names only the immediate predecessor (#768). But #768 depends on #766 (TASK-C548-2, "≥10 curated circuits ship under `resources/samples/`"), which depends on #764 (TASK-C548-1, Examples menu), which depends on #381. `resources/samples/` does not exist in this checkout (`Glob resources/samples/**` returns nothing; #381's own O3 confirms: "`resources/samples/` does not exist today"). So #773's outcome ("one scripted command renders an SVG for every circuit in the Examples set") currently has zero circuits to enumerate. That's a legitimate use of `ordering_after`, but the issue gives no hint that the actual gating work is three unstarted issues deep, which is a planning/estimation hazard for whoever picks this up expecting only #768 to land first.

**3. [Medium] AC3 ("no second copy of any caption text") is in tension with #768's own spec, and the metadata schema it depends on doesn't exist yet.**
#768 (TASK-C548-3) AC4 requires the caption to *also* be embedded "in the opened circuit itself (a header `Text` element or equivalent)" for someone who opens the file outside the menu/gallery. That is a second textual rendering of the same caption by design — one in circuit-file `Text` geometry, one in whatever structured metadata #548's set defines for programmatic reads. #773's AC3 doesn't say which of these is the single source of truth the gallery script must read from, or how the two are kept from drifting apart (a stale in-circuit `Text` element next to an updated metadata caption is exactly a "second copy," and nothing in #773 or #768 tests that they match). Worse, the metadata format itself is not yet defined — #768 is still open and unstarted — so #773's AC3 is written against a schema that doesn't exist, making the criterion currently unverifiable rather than merely unmet.
Recommendation: name the metadata source of truth explicitly (presumably #768's structured format, not the in-circuit `Text`), and add a check that the in-circuit caption and the metadata caption agree, or state why that's out of scope.

**4. [Low] AC1/AC2 as written are satisfiable by an implementation that never checks correctness of the output, only its self-consistency.**
"One command renders an SVG plus caption for every circuit" plus "CI ... fails when a committed render differs from the freshly generated one" together only assert idempotence of the script against itself — a script that pairs the wrong caption with the wrong circuit, or emits placeholder/blank SVGs, still satisfies both criteria as long as it does so deterministically. Nothing in the stated ACs asserts that a given SVG's filename/id ties unambiguously to the circuit it was rendered from and to the correct caption. This is likely caught in practice by #551's higher-level ACs (browsable gallery, README links), but as a standalone task card the acceptance criteria don't rule out a gameable implementation.
Recommendation: add a criterion asserting circuit-to-render-to-caption identity (e.g., filename derived from circuit id, and a test iterating the Examples set asserting one SVG + one caption exists per entry with no orphans/extras).

**5. [Low] Output location/format and publish mechanism are unspecified.**
"emits the gallery's asset set" and "runs in CI or the release flow" don't name an output directory, file naming convention, or whether this produces raw assets only vs. an HTML page (the HTML page and its hosting are #551's job, per the boundary notes, so this is likely intentional under-specification) — but no GitHub Pages workflow exists yet in `.github/workflows/`, so "runs in CI" doesn't yet have a publish target to run *in*. Minor since #773 is explicitly scoped to generation only, but worth flagging so the task isn't picked up assuming a hosting pipeline already exists.

## What's solid

- AC1 correctly reuses shipped, tested machinery (`-i out.svg`, issue #154, covered by `SvgExportTest`/`CliImageExportTest`) rather than inventing new export logic — low implementation risk on that half.
- AC3's intent (captions live in #548's metadata, not duplicated in the gallery) is the right instinct even though its current wording is unverifiable pre-#768 (finding 3).
- AC4's boundary note explicitly disclaims blocking on #536 and disclaims duplicating its styling work — a clean, well-drawn scope line that prevents this task from ballooning into the print-styling feature.
- The overall shape (generation vs. presentation split between #773 and #551) is sound task decomposition; the problem is in AC2's determinism assumption, not the split itself.

## Verdict rationale

`needs-rework`: the core mechanism (reuse `-i out.svg`, drive from #548 metadata) is reasonable, but AC2 as written bakes in a byte-identical-across-machines guarantee that the codebase's own tests document as false for this export path, and that the project itself is funding separately (and at ~5-8x the band) under #536. That should be resolved — either by descoping the diff check or by taking on the determinism dependency explicitly — before implementation starts, or the CI gate this task builds will be flaky by construction.
